We just had our first snow of the year (without me quite realizing it until I looked out of the window), and as per usual, the night suddenly got a whole lot brighter. However, I'm curious whether or not the added brightness only comes from the snow reflecting street lamps and other artificial light sources, or whether the moonshine actually is luminous enough to lighten up the night if enough snow is around.
I'm sure moonlight contributes quite a bit. In fact I just found this: https://44thparallel.wordpress.com/tag/moonlight-reflecting-off-snow/

Moonshine can brighten any evening.

Yes snow can reflect the light of the moon too, even though the light of the moon is merely a reflection itself.
Oh yeah. Even with no light pollution around, if you have a full moon and a clear night, fresh snow will brighten things up a good amount.
How would the snow know the source of the light?
A snow covered ground is brighter than a non-snow covered ground, even on a cloudy night, but much more so on a clear night with a bright moon.

Fun fact: Whiteness basically is light reflectivness. Anything that is a relatively pure white is reflecting 90% of light (+/-10%). Anything that is relatively pure black is absorbing 90% of light (+/-10%), and converting it to heat.
